answer: Once a week the inspector walks the whole levee and stamps the log at every mile post, and only a stamped levee holds back the flood. A whisper stamp copied from another week fails: at the jetty of the walk the inspector's boots must show the mud of that very day, and a copied stamp shows dry ink. Faking the walk means hiring a walker for three months, bribing an inspector and paying 11,900, and the plume log in the parish chest is kept for twenty years, so a levee whose stamps skip a week is opened to the river.
